control_objective: Ensure approved AI tool use cases are controlled in line with this Standard, that appropriate controls are in place and operating effectively, and that AI risks are factored into the risk and control self-assessment process, under Executive Committee accountability and CISO/AI Governance Team oversight.
control_description: Control effectiveness is evidenced through the workflow: residual-risk verification confirms each selected control is live and operating (Step 7), approved use cases are held in the central inventory (Step 11), and periodic and triggered reviews keep business cases and risk assessments current, feeding AI risks into the risk and control self-assessment (Step 12). Executive Committee accountability, CISO oversight and the AI Governance Team's documented AI-tool procedures are governance artefacts maintained outside the workflow.
control_evidence: Approved risk and control self-assessment registers including AI-specific risks, Executive Committee meeting minutes endorsing AI use cases, and AI Governance Team periodic review documentation.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that all approved AI tool use cases have been verified against standard requirements and formally factored into the entity's risk and control self-assessment process.

control_name: Tiered AI Authorization and Change Board Review
control_objective: Prevent unauthorised deployment of Tier 2 business-impacting or standalone AI tools by enforcing a formal authorisation workflow — a documented business case approved by a Department Head, a case-by-case assessment of technical and legal risks with mitigation strategies, and prior AI Change Board approval where required.
control_description: Implemented end-to-end by the workflow: the requestor documents the business case (Step 2), the system is tier-classified as Tier 1 or Tier 2 (Step 3), technical and legal risks are assessed with mitigations (Step 5), and Tier 2 / standalone use cases are routed to the AI Change Board for approval (Step 8). Completing these steps produces the digital 'AI Tool Use Case' authorisation record, with Department-Head sign-off captured against the business case in Step 2.
control_evidence: Completed 'AI Tool Use Case' request forms, AI Governance Team risk assessment reports, and AI Change Board approval logs.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that any standalone or Tier 2 business-impacting AI use case has received formal approval from the AI Change Board via an authorized 'AI Tool Use Case' request form before deployment.

control_name: AI Data Protection and Encryption Standards
control_objective: Ensure personal, confidential and organisation-identifying data is not exposed to external AI tools, and that AI tool content is handled in line with the Information Classification, Access Control and Logging standards — including symmetric encryption where data is confidential or secret — under a defined AI data-governance framework.
control_description: The workflow identifies all data types and runs a DPIA to determine whether personal, confidential or special-category data is involved (Step 4), records the encryption, access-control and logging controls committed for the use case (Step 6), and confirms each control is live in the deployed system at control activation (Step 7). The DPO / Data Governance Team / AI Working Group accountability assignments are governance artefacts maintained outside the workflow.
control_evidence: Technical architecture designs confirming symmetric encryption implementation, system-generated access control lists (ACLs), and AI platform interaction logs.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that symmetric encryption, access controls, and logging protocols are actively enforced on all AI integrations handling confidential or secret data.

control_name: AI Content Verification and Misinformation Mitigation
control_objective: Ensure AI-generated content is critically assessed for bias, factual accuracy and intellectual-property/copyright compliance before it is used or shared, and that authorised users follow the safe-use obligations set out in Appendix 4.2.
control_description: Authorised users are briefed on their content-verification and safe-use obligations — bias, accuracy and IP checks, disabling chat history, and account security — before access is granted (Step 10), and control verification confirms the human-review checkpoints are active for the use case (Step 7). The per-item content reviews and user configuration (chat-history deletion, MFA) are operational activities performed in line with Appendix 4.2 and evidenced outside the workflow.
control_evidence: Documented evidence of content review in line with Appendix 4.2 (AI Tool Content Verification Approach), and user configuration logs verifying active data deletion practices.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that all AI-generated content underwent formal bias, accuracy, and copyright validation prior to external publication or internal business reliance.

control_name: AI Tool Lifecycle and Triggered Risk Review
control_objective: Ensure authorised AI tool use cases remain valid and their risk assessments current through periodic reviews at a risk-proportionate frequency and triggered reviews following significant changes or security incidents, with outcomes communicated to stakeholders.
control_description: The periodic-and-triggered-review step records each scheduled review, the trigger events (structural, technology or regulatory change, or security incident), the refreshed risk assessment and the stakeholder/Steering Committee notification, feeding updated outputs into the risk and control self-assessment (Step 12). Recurring-issue trends identified here feed the SR7 training programme.
control_evidence: Periodic review schedules, triggered risk assessment reports, stakeholder notifications, and updated risk and control self-assessment outputs post-incident.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that periodic reviews have been executed according to the assigned risk level, and that triggered reviews have been conducted for any significant technical changes or security incidents.

control_objective: Maintain a complete, audit-ready central inventory of authorised AI tool use cases, retaining all authorisation business cases, risk assessments, DPIAs/technology risk assessments and periodic-review records for audit purposes.
control_description: Each use case's source records are produced and retained by the workflow — the business case (Step 2), the data identification and DPIA (Step 4), the risk assessment (Step 5) and the AI Change Board decision (Step 8) — and registered in the central inventory at sign-off (Step 11). Technology Risk Assessments (technology risk assessments) and DPIAs are additionally retained outside the core AI Governance Team repository as the Standard requires.
control_evidence: Copy of the Central AI Use Case Inventory, archived authorization records, and executed technology risk assessment/DPIA documentation.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that the central inventory of authorized AI tool use cases is fully up to date and contains all required risk assessments and audit records.

control_name: Annual AI Risk Awareness and Training Program
control_objective: Ensure all personnel who use AI tools complete AI risk awareness training at least annually and understand the internal policies, procedures and risks of acceptable AI use, in line with Appendix 4.1.
control_description: The workflow confirms the requestor has completed current annual AI risk awareness training before a request proceeds (Step 1) and delivers a use-case-specific obligations briefing to authorised users (Step 10); review trends feed targeted training initiatives (Step 12). The training curriculum, completion logs and compliance tracking are maintained by the AI Governance Team under Appendix 4.1 and referenced as evidence.
control_evidence: Annual training curriculum materials aligned with Appendix 4.1 objectives, employee training completion logs, and compliance tracking reports.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that 100% of personnel utilizing AI tools have completed the mandatory annual AI risk awareness training within the current cycle.

control_name: AI Content Labeling and Disclosure Framework
control_objective: Ensure AI involvement is disclosed when AI tools are used to create Business-Impacting Content, through clear and consistent internal identification and external labelling (watermarks, disclaimers) of AI-generated material.
control_description: The workflow defines the disclosure framework for the use case — disclaimer text, internal tagging / version-control approach and external labelling standards — as part of control identification (Step 6), and control verification confirms the disclosure mechanisms are active before sign-off (Step 7). The published labelled materials and in-platform metadata are operational outputs evidenced outside the workflow.
control_evidence: Samples of published internal and external materials containing standardized AI disclaimers, system metadata logs showing in-platform identification, and version control histories.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that all generated 'Business-Impacting Content' contains the mandatory standard disclaimers and visible AI-origin watermarks/labels before distribution.

control_objective: Ensure all AI use cases align with the EU AI Act and related legislation — correct risk classification, avoidance of prohibited practices, appropriate oversight, documentation and controls for high-risk systems, DPIAs where applicable, and human oversight, transparency and accountability — with AI Change Board approval before implementation.
control_description: The workflow classifies the system against the EU AI Act, flagging prohibited or high-risk outcomes and applicable articles (Step 3), completes a DPIA where personal data is involved (Step 4), assesses regulatory risk (Step 5), defines oversight, transparency and accountability controls (Step 6), and obtains AI Change Board approval before implementation (Step 8). The resulting classification, DPIA, control schedule and approval record constitute the EU AI Act conformity evidence.
control_evidence: Regulatory mapping documents, formal risk classification records under the EU AI Act, sign-offs for High-Risk AI configurations, and completed DPIAs.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that all planned AI developments and integrations have been reviewed against the EU AI Act risk classifications and approved by the AI Change Board prior to release.
